records.name: Dearnley Park Civic Association
records.summary: Dearnley Park neighbors who meet on Zoom to review zoning board requests and city projects, such as a water main replacement, and speak up for the area. The group has also talked about cleanup projects with a neighboring association.
records.what_you_do: Members review zoning board applications and city construction projects at quarterly Zoom meetings and vote on the group's position. Officers are elected to two-year terms.

schedule.text: Quarterly meetings on Zoom at 7 pm, held on a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday.

cost.text: Household membership is $20 a year and business membership is $50 a year. The site lists no fee to attend meetings.

first_step.how: Join the next quarterly Zoom meeting at 7 pm using the link on the homepage. The site lists October 14, 2026 as the next meeting, with a zoning board request on the agenda.
first_step.basis: The homepage says any resident may join the Zoom meetings through the posted link, and no sign-up is described. Membership is for people who live or run a business in Dearnley Park.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings are online at 7 pm and follow a set agenda, such as a zoning board review and a water department project on the Ridge Avenue corridor. Members vote on the group's position and elect officers every two years. The site lists no fee to attend, and household dues are $20 a year if you choose to join.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the date by email first, because the homepage lists both September 30 and October 14, 2026 as the next meeting.
Membership is for residents or business owners of Dearnley Park, and dues are paid by check or money order to the treasurer.
Have the Zoom link from the homepage ready before 7 pm.

records.notes: The homepage shows two next-meeting dates (September 30 and October 14, 2026) and still has summer text, so the site may be behind. The phone number changed from the City list number (267-225-0914) to the number the group publishes on its homepage and contact page (267-241-7476). The treasurer's mailing address on the membership section is a private home, so it was left out. The contact page names no contact person; the tier 1 name is kept, and the group's June 2026 officer notice lists Dot French as president.

records.name: East Falls Community Council
records.summary: An all-volunteer nonprofit, incorporated in 1975, that speaks for East Falls residents on zoning, development and neighborhood issues. It meets monthly and holds open forums, such as a candidates night before local elections.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in East Falls and talk them over at the monthly meeting. Membership also brings a weekly events email, and only members vote at meetings.

schedule.text: Monthly council meetings on the second Monday of each month, open to all East Falls neighbors.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: East Falls Presbyterian Church, 3800 Vaux Street, Philadelphia, PA 19129

cost.text: Member dues are $10 a year and supporting dues are $25. Higher donor levels are named after offices and run from $50 to $500.

first_step.how: Come to the next monthly meeting on the second Monday, or to the October 12, 2026 candidates night, which the site says is open to all. Join as a member through the online form if you want to vote.
first_step.basis: The site says council meetings are open to all East Falls neighbors and links an online membership form. It does not describe a newcomer welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings take place once a month on the second Monday, and any neighbor can sit in. Only current members vote, and member dues start at $10 a year. The October 2026 meeting is a candidates night where candidates or their representatives answer questions.
first_visit_tips: The site's listing for October 12, 2026 gives a 7 pm start but no room, so email info@eastfallscommunity.org to ask where it is held.
Membership is joined through an online form linked from the Join Us button, and the group's P.O. Box is on the site for mail.

records.notes: Tier 1 used the group's Facebook page as its website. The group's own site is eastfallscommunity.org, now the website, and Facebook is kept under social. The tier 1 email (a personal address) was replaced with the group's published info address, and the tier 1 contact name is kept. The site gives no start time for regular meetings apart from the October 12, 2026 candidates night at 7 pm, so no time is set in schedule. One web search returned 2015 to 2018 newspaper notices with an older meeting time and venue; those were not used as facts. The same search named a second East Falls council, East Falls Forward, which is listed in leads_only.

records.name: Residents of Shawmont Valley Association
records.summary: A neighborhood association for upper Roxborough, founded in 1980, that works to protect local greenways, waterways and the watershed and speaks up on zoning and quality of life. Members meet a few times a year and help with a spring street cleanup.
records.what_you_do: Members attend meetings and vote on the association's positions, follow watershed and gully projects with partner groups, and turn out for the spring street cleanup on Shawmont Avenue.

schedule.text: Meets semi-regularly and as needed for zoning matters. A Spring Street Cleanup on Shawmont Avenue is held each April on a Saturday morning.

cost.text: Dues are $10 for one person or $15 for a two-person household.

first_step.how: Sign up for the site's low-volume email updates, then come to the next Spring Street Cleanup on Shawmont Avenue, where it meets Minerva.
first_step.basis: The site does not say whether non-members can come to meetings, and membership comes with $10 to $15 in dues. The email list and the spring cleanup are the only clear ways in.
first_step.what_to_expect: The spring cleanup gathers on Shawmont Avenue on a Saturday morning in April, and past ones started at 9 or 10 am. Meetings happen semi-regularly and as needed, and recent ones were held at Roxborough Presbyterian Church on Ridge Avenue. Members can attend meetings and vote, and dues can be paid in cash or by check.
first_visit_tips: The events page still lists an April 11, 2026 cleanup as upcoming, so email the group to confirm the next date.
Email the group before a first meeting to ask whether non-members can attend.
Subscribe to the site's email list or RSS feed to hear about meetings.

records.notes: The events page is out of date: its newest dated item is the April 11, 2026 cleanup, still labeled upcoming, so last_sign_of_life uses April 2026. The City RCO list dates the record 2026-10, but that is a registry entry, not dated activity by the group. The join page gives a private street address as the place to drop off dues; that address was left out. The homepage says joining lets members attend meetings and vote, but the site does not say whether non-members may attend. The feed link is the group's own RSS feed.

records.name: Ridge Park Civic Association
records.summary: A volunteer-run, non-partisan community group for the Roxborough and Manayunk area since 1995. It reviews zoning requests, plants street trees, organizes neighborhood cleanups, and supports historic preservation.
records.what_you_do: Members come to quarterly meetings, where developers and officials sometimes present, and volunteers join cleanups in Germany Hill, plant trees through the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society's program, or help the preservation committee.

schedule.text: Quarterly general meetings, usually on the second Tuesday of March, June, September and December at 7 pm, held in person or on Zoom. Cleanups run through the year.

cost.text: Annual dues are $15 for one person, $25 for a household, $10 for one person age 65 and over, $15 for a household age 65 and over, and $65 for a business.

first_step.how: Stop by a neighborhood cleanup in Germany Hill. The volunteer page says anyone can join cleanups, weekly or occasionally.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says a first-timer can arrive at a cleanup without registering first, and the homepage invites new neighbors to join, volunteer or get involved. The site describes no separate newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Cleanups remove trash and debris in Germany Hill and nearby areas, working with the Roxborough Manayunk Conservancy and Ivy Ridge Green, and they happen through the year. Quarterly meetings are open to members and guests, and recent ones were held both in person and on Zoom. Dues can be paid in person at a meeting or through PayPal.
first_visit_tips: The cleanup schedule link on the volunteer page is labeled 2020, so ask the group which cleanup is next before you go.
Recent quarterly meetings were held in person and on Zoom, so check which format the next one uses.
If you want to help with historic preservation, contact the preservation committee first, since the page asks people to reach out before joining.

records.notes: Recent meetings: June 9, 2026 in person at a Ridge Avenue venue, and September 8, 2026 on Zoom. The venue is not recorded because the site names a business and the format changes, so the tier 1 location (Zoom) is kept. The homepage's Designer Bag Bingo (October 16, 2026) is a fundraiser, so it is noted here and not in the schedule. The cleanup schedule link is labeled 2020 and may be stale. The board list was not visible on the pages read. Added nature-environment and history categories and the park cleanup, tree tending and preservation interests from the group's own program list.

records.name: Roxborough Development Corporation
records.summary: The Roxborough development group that runs and promotes public neighborhood events, such as the Roxtoberfest street festival, and keeps a local news and events page and business directory. The City also lists it as a registered community organization.
records.what_you_do: The group runs and promotes public events, including the fall Roxtoberfest street festival, and its events page lists a monthly still life drawing workshop. Local businesses and makers can become vendors or sponsors, and the site invites people to sign up for its newsletter.

schedule.text: Roxtoberfest is a yearly street festival on Ridge Avenue each fall, and the events page lists a monthly still life drawing workshop.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on the group's site, then come to a public event such as Roxtoberfest, held on Ridge Avenue each fall.
first_step.basis: Festivals and workshops listed on the site are open to the public, and the site invites people to sign up for its newsletter. The site does not describe membership or resident meetings.
first_step.what_to_expect: The 2026 Roxtoberfest ran noon to 6 pm on Ridge Avenue, with live music on three stages, beer gardens, food, a dog costume parade and a wellness village with health screenings. The site calls it a community and family festival and says it draws more than 10,000 visitors. The site does not say whether admission is free.
first_visit_tips: Many listings give only a date, so check the events page close to the day for the time and place.
Email info@roxboroughpa.com with questions about cost or tickets before a workshop or event.
If you run a business or make things to sell, ask about vendor and sponsor spots by email; the site sends those questions to a named staff member.

records.notes: This is a festival, events and business promotion site. No page read describes zoning review, membership or resident meetings, so the tier 1 zoning sentence was removed from what_you_do. The City list still shows it as a registered community organization, and that is kept in the summary. The tier 1 email was a staff member's address from the City list; the group's published info address is used instead. The about-us and who-we-are pages returned 404, so the mission was not confirmed. Dated events with no stated time or price (ROX Crit on October 1 and Pocket Park After Dark on October 22, 2026) were left out of schedule. The October 6, 2026 blog post is the newest dated item.

records.name: Upper Roxborough Civic Association
records.summary: The volunteer civic association for Upper Roxborough and a registered community organization. It meets every second Wednesday at Roxborough Church, and new neighbors are welcome to come to a meeting and get to know the board.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors meet with the board to talk over neighborhood matters, pay dues of $25 per household or $50 per business, and volunteer, especially on fundraising, events and technology.

schedule.text: Meets every second Wednesday at 6:30 pm at Roxborough Church, with no meetings in July or August unless a pressing issue comes up.

cost.text: Household dues are $25 a year and business dues are $50 a year. Dues can be paid at a meeting or arranged by email.

first_step.how: Come to a meeting at Roxborough Church, 8230 Ridge Ave, at 6:30 pm and introduce yourself to the board.
first_step.basis: The homepage says a new neighbor can come to a meeting and get to know the board, and it gives the meeting day, time and place.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings are held at Roxborough Church on Ridge Avenue at 6:30 pm, and the board is introduced on the homepage. Dues of $25 a household or $50 a business can be paid at a meeting. The site does not say how long meetings run or whether they can be joined online.
first_visit_tips: The site has no calendar, so email the group to confirm the next meeting date before you go.
Membership applications use an online form linked from the homepage.
Dues can be paid at a meeting, or you can email to arrange another way to pay.

records.notes: The homepage gives meetings every second Wednesday at 6:30 pm at Roxborough Church, plus dues and board names. The events, news and contact pages show no dated items and no phone or email, so the tier 1 contact details are kept from the City list. Status is probably_active rather than active because the site has no dated notices. The last sign of life is the City RCO list date, the only dated item found. The tier 1 meeting place (Zoom and VI Rec Center) was replaced with the church named on the group's own site, and the site does not mention Zoom. The site says 'every second Wednesday' without saying whether that means every two weeks or the second Wednesday of each month, so confirm by email. The tier 1 zoning sentence was removed from what_you_do because the site does not describe zoning review; the City list still shows it as a registered community organization.
